Package com.nexuslink.protocol.http.rest

Class CacheControl

java.lang.Object
com.nexuslink.protocol.http.rest.CacheControl
public final class CacheControl extends Object
Pure, dependency-free parser and model for an HTTP Cache-Control header as defined by RFC 7234 §5.2.

A Cache-Control header carries a comma-separated list of cache directives. Each directive is a token, optionally followed by = and an argument that is either a token or a quoted string: 


   Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable
   Cache-Control: no-cache="Set-Cookie", private
   Cache-Control: max-age=30, s-maxage=60

Directives fall into three groups:

  • Boolean directives that stand alone: no-cache, no-store, no-transform, only-if-cached, must-revalidate, public, private, proxy-revalidate, immutable, must-understand.
  • Value directives carrying a delta-seconds argument: max-age, s-maxage, max-stale, min-fresh, stale-while-revalidate, stale-if-error. Per RFC 7234 §5.2.1.2 max-stale may appear with no value, meaning "any" freshness overrun is acceptable.
  • Some directives (no-cache, private) may instead carry a quoted field list naming header fields, e.g. no-cache="Set-Cookie". The unquoted argument is captured verbatim and reachable via directive(String).

Directive names are case-insensitive and stored lower-cased. Every directive — recognised or not — is preserved in a generic name→argument map, where the argument is null for a directive that appeared without an = value. Unknown directives are therefore kept rather than rejected, which lets callers inspect vendor extensions.

Parsing is lenient: a malformed comma-separated element (an empty name, or a value directive whose argument is not a valid delta-seconds) is tolerated — the raw text is still stored, and typed numeric accessors simply report the value as absent rather than throwing. Quoted arguments may themselves contain commas and semicolons without being mistaken for separators. When a directive repeats, the first occurrence wins. Passing null or a blank string yields an empty result in which every directive is absent.

The class performs no network or file I/O and is fully offline-testable. Instances are immutable.

  • Method Details

    • parse

      public static CacheControl parse(String input)
      Parses a Cache-Control header value into its directives.

      Multiple Cache-Control header lines from a message may be joined with commas and passed as a single string. Parsing is lenient (see the class documentation).

      Parameters:
      input - the raw Cache-Control header value; may be null or blank
      Returns:
      an immutable CacheControl holding the parsed directives (possibly empty)

    • directives

      public Map<String,String> directives()
      All parsed directives, keyed by lower-cased name, in first-seen order. A null value marks a directive that appeared without an = argument. Never null, possibly empty; unmodifiable.

    • directive

      public String directive(String name)
      The raw argument of the named directive, matched case-insensitively.
      Parameters:
      name - directive name (e.g. "max-age"); may be null
      Returns:
      the argument text, or null if the directive is absent or present without a value — use has(String) to distinguish the two cases

    • has

      public boolean has(String name)
      Whether the named directive is present (case-insensitive), regardless of whether it carried a value.
      Parameters:
      name - directive name; may be null
      Returns:
      true if the directive appeared in the header

    • toString

      public String toString()
      Re-renders the directives as a Cache-Control header value. Directives are emitted in first-seen order, comma-separated. A directive with no value is rendered bare; a value that contains whitespace, a comma or a quote is emitted as a quoted string (with embedded quotes and backslashes escaped), otherwise it is emitted as a bare token. The result round-trips back through parse(String).
